Sadly, this is not unprecedented.

W and Obama initiated bailouts of GM and Chrysler. Carter did it for Chrysler before. FDR certainly used all kinds of powers during ww2 to control/direct corporations and even appointments to businesses. Congress regularly picks winners and losers (look at the massive amount of stock winnings Congress has, while they're exempted from insider trading rules unlike the rest of us).

If you go further back in time.. many Presidents have nationalized (partially or full) companies, Herbert Hoover urged companies to raise wages, JFK publicly attacked US Steel, Truman issued an executive order to sieze control of Steel companies in 1952, etc..

As long as we keep voting for more government, and Congress keeps expanding the powers of the Executive Branch, this is what we're going to get more of..

This is nothing to do with "more government", that precisely what Trump is against -- he wants to remove regulations to let industry run free people like him make lots of money.

Which is exactly what he's doing here -- he *loves* backing winners (whether legally or not), especially if he profits as a direct result. Massively in this case, not just his Nvidia shares but all the other ways he makes money from stock market rises/falls.

Corruption and nepotism, pure and simple, those are the founding principles that drive Trump. He couldn't give a rat's ass about legalities or principles, those are for LOSERS...

IMO, The more powerful the government is, the more likely this sort of thing is going to happen. Congress does this corruption all of the time, but it gets hand waved it as "a few bad actors". Well, more actors = more bad actors..

Note this is not a defense of Trump at all, I think his economic and foreign policies are absolutely terrible. But he IS a symptom of the system..

If we hand wave this away as "Trump is bad" then we'll never fix the root cause of these kinds of happenings.
